# Incident Report: STRRAT RAT Infection — DESKTOP-SKBR25F

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames, ~582 sec capture). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived directly from packet analysis with tshark.

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| Logged-in user | ccollier (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString to the domain controller and via the malware's own beacon field) |
| OS (self-reported by malware) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |
| AD domain / DC | wiresharkworkshop.online, DC = WIRESHARK-WS-DC (172.16.1.4, MAC 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35) — legitimate lab AD infrastructure, not an IOC |

## Malware Family

**STRRAT** — a Java-based remote access trojan.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The C2 beacon protocol contains the literal, unencrypted string `STRRAT` in every check-in message (frame 9119 onward), e.g.:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|1 Sec
```

This is STRRAT's known plaintext pipe-delimited beacon format: `ping|<family>|<campaign/build ID>|<hostname>|<username>|<OS>|<arch>|<AV product>|<active window (base64)>|<version>|<geo>|<flag>|<uptime>`. Later beacons in the same stream (e.g. frame ~9600+) include an active-window field `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` (base64) = `Program Manager`, consistent with STRRAT's window-title reporting. Reported STRRAT client version: **1.6**. Campaign/build ID: **1BE8292C**.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control endpoint:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` (TCP) — plaintext STRRAT ping protocol, no TLS. First contact at t=76.99s (frame 9066), beacon interval ~5 seconds, continuing uninterrupted through the end of the capture (t=585.66s). This IP was never resolved via DNS in the capture — the malware connects to it directly by hardcoded IP, a strong C2 indicator.

**Supporting/reconnaissance indicator:**
- `ip-api.com` (resolved to 208.95.112.1) — HTTP GET `/json/` at frame 9111, returning geolocation JSON (`countryCode: US, region: TX, city: Austin`). This matches the `US:United States` geo field the malware subsequently reports in its beacon, confirming the malware performs a self-geolocation lookup as part of its check-in routine.

**Malicious domains:** None observed. The C2 channel uses a raw IP (141.98.10.79) with no associated DNS query in this capture, so no malicious domain can be grounded in the evidence.

**Malicious URLs:** None observed. The C2 protocol on port 12132 is a raw TCP pipe-delimited beacon, not HTTP — no URL is used for C2.

**Transferred files / hashes:** None observed. The capture begins with the host already on the network (NBNS name release/registration at t=0) and the STRRAT beacon is already active by t=77s; no initial-access payload delivery (dropper, JAR, LNK, MSI) appears in this capture. All contact with `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) and `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (23.194.164.136) — plausible Java runtime dependencies for a Java-based RAT — is TLS-encrypted, so no file name or SHA256 can be extracted from this pcap alone.

## Summary

172.16.1.66 (DESKTOP-SKBR25F, user ccollier) is actively beaconing to an external STRRAT C2 server at 141.98.10.79:12132 for the full duration of the capture, at ~5-second intervals, in cleartext. The malware performed a geolocation self-check via ip-api.com. No lateral movement or additional C2 channels were observed from this host; all other outbound activity (Microsoft/Office 365, MSN, Bing, GitHub, Maven Central, Oracle Java) is consistent with normal Windows 11/Office telemetry and background services. Recommended action: isolate 172.16.1.66, block 141.98.10.79/12132 at the perimeter, and reset ccollier's credentials pending full host forensics (memory/disk) to recover the STRRAT dropper and confirm persistence mechanism.
